python-basics.title: Python Foundations
python-basics.description: Python syntax, types, collections and core programming concepts.

questions.question: Which Python type is mutable?
questions.explanation: A list can be changed after creation; tuples, strings and integers cannot.

questions.question: What does len([4, 5, 6]) return?
questions.explanation: The list contains three elements.

questions.question: Which keyword starts a function definition?
questions.explanation: Python uses def to define a named function.

questions.question: What is the result of 7 // 2?
questions.explanation: // performs floor division; seven divided by two rounds down to three.

questions.question: What does a Python dictionary store?
questions.explanation: Dictionaries associate unique keys with values.

questions.question: Which expression creates a set?
questions.explanation: Curly braces with values create a set; repeated values are deduplicated.

questions.question: Which statement handles an exception?
questions.explanation: Python uses try and except for exception handling.

questions.question: What is printed by print(2 ** 3)?
questions.explanation: ** is exponentiation, so 2 cubed is 8.

questions.question: What does range(3) generate when iterated?
questions.explanation: range(3) starts at zero and stops before three.

questions.question: Which method adds one item to the end of a list?
questions.explanation: list.append(value) adds a single element to the end.

sql-basics.title: SQL Foundations
sql-basics.description: Filtering, aggregation, joins and relational query basics.

questions.question: Which statement retrieves rows from a table?
questions.explanation: SELECT retrieves data from one or more tables.

questions.question: Which clause filters rows before grouping?
questions.explanation: WHERE filters input rows before GROUP BY aggregates them.

questions.question: Which clause sorts output rows?
questions.explanation: ORDER BY orders rows by one or more expressions.

questions.question: What does COUNT(*) return?
questions.explanation: COUNT(*) counts rows including rows containing NULL values.

questions.question: Which join returns matching rows from both sides?
questions.explanation: INNER JOIN returns rows satisfying the join condition on both sides.

questions.question: What does GROUP BY generally do?
questions.explanation: GROUP BY groups matching key values for aggregate calculations.

questions.question: Which predicate checks a missing SQL value?
questions.explanation: NULL is checked with IS NULL rather than = NULL.

questions.question: Which function calculates the mean of a numeric column?
questions.explanation: AVG computes the arithmetic mean of non-NULL values.

questions.question: Which clause filters aggregated groups?
questions.explanation: HAVING filters groups after aggregation.

questions.question: Which keyword removes duplicate result rows?
questions.explanation: SELECT DISTINCT removes duplicate rows from the output.

indian-polity.title: Indian Polity — UPSC Practice
indian-polity.description: Constitution, institutions and civic governance fundamentals.

questions.question: Which part of the Constitution contains Fundamental Rights?
questions.explanation: Fundamental Rights are primarily contained in Part III.

questions.question: Who is the constitutional head of the Union executive?
questions.explanation: The President is the constitutional head of the Union executive.

questions.question: Who presides over the Rajya Sabha ex officio?
questions.explanation: India’s Vice-President is the ex officio Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: Which article establishes the Election Commission of India?
questions.explanation: Article 324 vests election superintendence, direction and control in the Election Commission.

questions.question: Directive Principles of State Policy are mainly in which part?
questions.explanation: Directive Principles of State Policy appear in Part IV.

questions.question: Who appoints the Prime Minister of India?
questions.explanation: The President appoints the Prime Minister.

questions.question: What is the minimum age for election to the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: A candidate for the Lok Sabha must be at least 25 years old.

questions.question: Which constitutional amendment introduced Panchayati Raj constitutional provisions?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment inserted Part IX concerning Panchayats.

questions.question: Which court is at the apex of the Indian judicial system?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court of India is the apex court.

questions.question: Which is a money bill introduction rule under the Constitution?
questions.explanation: A Money Bill may only be introduced in the Lok Sabha.

indian-history.title: Indian History — UPSC Practice
indian-history.description: Major periods and foundational events of Indian history.

questions.question: The Maurya Empire was founded by whom?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya established the Maurya dynasty.

questions.question: Which ancient site is known for the Great Bath?
questions.explanation: The Great Bath is a well-known structure at Mohenjo-daro.

questions.question: Who wrote the Arthashastra traditionally attributed to Kautilya?
questions.explanation: The Arthashastra is traditionally attributed to Kautilya, also known as Chanakya.

questions.question: The Mughal Empire in India was founded by whom?
questions.explanation: Babur founded the Mughal Empire following the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.

questions.question: The Battle of Plassey took place in which year?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Plassey was fought in 1757.

questions.question: Who led the Salt March in 1930?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi led the Salt March as an act of civil disobedience.

questions.question: Which event began in Meerut in May 1857?
questions.explanation: The major uprising of 1857 began among sepoys in Meerut.

questions.question: The Indian National Congress was founded in which year?
questions.explanation: The Indian National Congress was established in 1885.

questions.question: Who was the first President of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: Womesh Chunder Bonnerjee presided over the first Congress session.

questions.question: Which movement was launched in August 1942?
questions.explanation: The Quit India Movement was launched in August 1942.

anatomy-basics.title: Human Anatomy Fundamentals
anatomy-basics.description: Introductory human anatomy concepts for medical learners.

questions.question: Which bone is the longest in the adult human body?
questions.explanation: The femur in the thigh is the longest bone.

questions.question: How many chambers does a typical human heart have?
questions.explanation: The human heart has two atria and two ventricles.

questions.question: Which organ lies primarily in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen?
questions.explanation: Most of the liver lies in the right upper abdomen.

questions.question: What is the main functional unit of the kidney?
questions.explanation: Nephrons are the kidney units that filter blood and process filtrate.

questions.question: Which body system includes the trachea?
questions.explanation: The trachea conducts air in the respiratory system.

questions.question: Which structure connects muscle to bone?
questions.explanation: Tendons connect muscles to bones; ligaments connect bones to bones.

questions.question: Which is the largest part of the human brain?
questions.explanation: The cerebrum is the largest major brain region.

questions.question: Which blood vessel carries blood from the heart to the lungs?
questions.explanation: Pulmonary arteries carry blood from the right ventricle toward the lungs.

questions.question: Which structure is the primary site of gas exchange in the lungs?
questions.explanation: Gas exchange occurs across alveolar and capillary membranes.

questions.question: Which part of the spine is located in the neck?
questions.explanation: The cervical spine forms the neck region.

physiology-basics.title: Human Physiology Fundamentals
physiology-basics.description: Basic organ functions, homeostasis and body processes.

questions.question: What is the main role of red blood cells?
questions.explanation: Hemoglobin in red blood cells carries oxygen.

questions.question: Which hormone primarily lowers blood glucose?
questions.explanation: Insulin promotes glucose uptake and storage, lowering blood glucose.

questions.question: Where does most nutrient absorption take place?
questions.explanation: Most nutrient absorption takes place in the small intestine.

questions.question: Which organ produces bile?
questions.explanation: The liver produces bile; the gallbladder stores and concentrates it.

questions.question: Which brain structure is important for balance and coordination?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum helps coordinate movement and balance.

questions.question: What is the principal function of platelets?
questions.explanation: Platelets help form hemostatic plugs during blood clotting.

questions.question: Which part of the nephron is a major site of filtration?
questions.explanation: Filtration occurs across the glomerular capillaries into Bowman’s capsule.

questions.question: Which hormone regulates water retention via kidney collecting ducts?
questions.explanation: ADH increases renal water reabsorption in the collecting ducts.

questions.question: During inhalation at rest, the diaphragm generally does what?
questions.explanation: Diaphragm contraction increases chest cavity volume, drawing air inward.

questions.question: Which region of the heart normally acts as the primary pacemaker?
questions.explanation: The sinoatrial node ordinarily initiates each heartbeat.
